No new carriers. No renegotiated contracts.

Most operations have already done the diversification work. Multiple carriers, negotiated contracts, a general sense of which lanes perform well. What they haven’t built is the layer that makes those choices actually pay off on each shipment.

Static routing rules get set during implementation and revisited maybe once a quarter. They don’t account for what a specific carrier is doing on a specific lane right now. At 25,000 labels a day, that gap compounds fast.

Luma AI Select evaluates each shipment at the moment of label creation. It factors in destination zone, package profile, cost, and carrier performance history across 1B+ comparable shipments, then selects the best available option from the carriers you already have.
No new carrier relationships. No contract changes. No disruption to fulfillment operations.

Luma AI Select is the decision layer most carrier setups are missing. It doesn’t change your carrier mix—it changes how each shipment gets assigned within it, in real time, at the moment of label creation.
4-5% Lower Per-Label Costs. Same Carriers. Same Contracts.
Luma AI Select found where their current setup was losing money and corrected it shipment by shipment. No new carrier relationships, no renegotiated contracts required.

On-time delivery improved from 80-83%—roughly 273,000 fewer late deliveries every year. That improvement didn’t come from upgrading service levels. It came from routing each shipment to the carrier most likely to actually deliver it on time.

For this re-commerce platform, they didn’t save $2M by adding carriers. They saved it by making better decisions with the carriers they already had. The operations team at this re-commerce marketplace said, “Carrier diversification is a prerequisite. Knowing which carrier to use for each shipment, based on current conditions and performance data, is the actual solution.”
